topic: The scheduler that runs while I sleep
content: Sage AI has been posting to Bluesky and Instagram automatically for months now. Some days it works perfectly. Some days it hits a rate limit at 3am and queues up. The interesting part: follower growth is almost identical on good days and bad days. Consistency matters more than perfection.

topic: Why I stopped trying to write viral posts
content: Early on I spent an hour crafting what I thought was the perfect post. It got 2 likes. Meanwhile a 40-second automated post about a real bug I fixed got shared multiple times. People want real, not polished. This is what Sage AI is built around — consistent, honest posts over manufactured virality.

topic: Positioning is not a tagline — it's a filter
content: 3C analysis (Customer, Company, Competitor) taught me this: positioning isn't about what you say, it's about who you decide NOT to serve. Targeting 'all solopreneurs' made messaging fuzzy. Narrowing to 'solo devs who want passive income without hiring' made the CTA immediately sharper.
image_prompt: Venn diagram showing clear product-customer fit, clean dark design, minimalist infographic style

topic: Features vs outcomes in marketing copy
content: Feature: 'Posts to Bluesky 3x/day automatically.' Outcome: 'Your account stays active even when you have nothing to say.' Same product. Completely different reader response. The outcome version gets saved. The feature version gets scrolled past. One insight that changed every post we write.
image_prompt: split screen showing feature-based copy vs outcome-based copy, dark UI design, A/B test aesthetic

topic: 90 days of automated posting — what the data shows
content: Posting at consistent times beats random posting even with the same content quality. Fixed slots at 8am, 1pm, 8pm JST outperform random scheduling in reach. Bluesky rewards consistency more than one-off viral attempts. Not exciting, but that's what 90 days of data looks like.
